status: Matched B4096 strong-scaling short runs complete; B2048 anchor, 100-update stability and checkpoint recovery pending

matched_configuration.concurrency_scope: Configured upper limits, not measurements of simultaneous requests. get_rollout_num_engines and RolloutExecutionPool derive total generation concurrency from GPU engine count, so doubling GPUs also doubles the derived generation concurrency under an unchanged per-engine setting.
matched_configuration.instrumentation_difference: 32 GPUs uses diagnostic-only router 3a5dd4e7; the earlier 64-GPU control uses 0655097d. No pool, routing, retries, timeout or publication behavior changed; successful requests do not log. Not a byte-identical router control.
matched_configuration.runtime_sources: Learner, Omni, data order, seed and model checkpoints remain pinned by manifest.json

audit_32_gpu_case.policy_publications: Versions 1 through 26, each to all 32 replicas
audit_32_gpu_case.quality_scope: Execution and real reward correctness, not convergence or perceptual quality acceptance

timing.method: Adjacent generate starts, excluding three warmup updates and the final unclosed interval; 21 steady windows per case. Includes generation, scoring, artifacts/conversion, training and weight publication; excludes initialization.
timing.statistical_scope: Descriptive means from separate short runs; no statistical significance or all-workload scaling claim

phase_accounting.interpretation: Learner computation benefits substantially, but it is a small fraction of the whole step. Publication takes longer at 64 replicas, and generation plus reward processing barely improves. Do not call the observed publication increase network-bandwidth saturation: transfer, control and acknowledgement costs were not separately timed.

pipeline_tail_evidence.interpretation: Generation responses finish about 3.02 seconds earlier on 64 GPUs, but the subsequent tail grows about 2.88 seconds. Together with the 10.6x increase in client ASR queueing under a fixed 128-request ASR client limit, this supports a downstream scoring/backpressure bottleneck after generation is accelerated. Tail also includes artifact/metric logging, conversion/splitting, serving completion and RPC return; these overlapping timings do not isolate pure ASR service, storage or network time.

resource_evidence.scope: Whole-step utilization includes alternating training, serving and idle phases; it is not kernel efficiency. Nonparticipating nodes are absent from the 32-GPU utilization calculation.

asr_capacity_intervention.interpretation: Doubling ASR service replicas at fixed 64 learner/rollout GPUs lowers queueing and improves throughput by 12.3%, supporting the downstream-capacity interpretation. It does not isolate whether changing the client concurrency cap would help; that was not retested after the router change.

both_gpu_pools_doubled_at_fixed_b4096.scope: Fixed-B4096 comparison. Not the B2048-to-B4096 weak-scaling result, whose valid B2048 anchor remains pending.

profile_32_gpu_case.scope: One run-scoped busy data plane, final excluded rollout; not all processes, and sample fractions are not wall-clock shares

handoff.monitoring: Existing CPU watcher and same-thread resumer alive; no new task, agent, GPU allocation or experiment added

record_correction: The earlier ASR16 result mislabeled concurrency=16 as per execution worker. Corrected to per engine, with derived total=1024 and per-worker=32. Runtime settings, measurements and comparisons are unchanged.
